 Sun Safety at UNSW: protect your skin this summer 
 06 Nov 2026
 Campus & Culture 
 Edition 21 2026 
 UNSW is launching a Sun Safety campaign to help staff stay protected this summer as UV levels continue to rise across Australia. 
 Skin cancer remains Australia's most common cancer.
 Did you know?
 two in three Australians will be diagnosed with skin cancer by age 70
 more than 440,000 Australians are treated for skin cancer each year
 most skin cancers are preventable and highly treatable when detected early. 
 What we offer
 UNSW is offering a range of initiatives including free on-site skin checks, SunSmart Hubs at participating campuses and a webinar where you will have access to practical tools and resources to support your skin health and reduce your risk of skin cancer.
 Free on-site skin checks
 UNSW has partnered with Medibank to offer free skin cancer checks on campus during work hours.
 As an added incentive, if you book and attend a skin check appointment you'll automatically go into the draw to win one of three $100 gift cards.
 Kensington campus  
 Monday 7 – Wednesday 9 December | UNSW HTH Room 1.224
Thursday 10 – Friday 11 December | H13 Lawrence West, Room 2035
 Book your appointment .
 Canberra ADFA campus  
 Tuesday 24 November | Building 36, Room 120
 Book your appointment .
 Canberra City campus 
 Wednesday 25 November | Building B01, Room 1.15
 Book your appointment .
 Sun Safety webinar
 Want to learn more about protecting yourself from Australia's harsh UV conditions?
 Join a 45-minute evidence-based webinar on Thursday 26 November at 1pm covering:
 how everyday UV exposure impacts long-term skin health
 how to conduct simple self-checks
 what happens during a professional skin check
 everyday sun protection strategies.
 You'll leave with practical, actionable steps you can use immediately to better protect yourself all year round.
 Register now .
 Visit a SunSmart Hub
 You can get free sunscreen and sun safe information at participating campuses throughout the campaign.  
 Whether you’re booking a skin check, joining the webinar or simply applying sunscreen before heading outside, small actions today can make a difference to your long-term health.
 This summer, take a moment to protect the skin you're in. Your future self will thank you for it.
